sections.content: How many people stayed in Lincoln after gaining qualifications?

Lincoln is a large town in the East Midlands. Lincoln also has a university.

Lincoln has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Lincoln ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 4,145 state-school pupils from Lincoln who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,040 (25%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,190 (29%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Lincoln to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Lincoln's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Lincoln in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Lincoln move to?

Of Lincoln's graduates, 480 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 110 of those graduates (23%) were living fairly locally, in the Lincoln travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Lincoln's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 330 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 180 of those qualified non-graduates (55%) were living fairly locally, in the Lincoln travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Lincoln's GCSE cohort:

  • 315 graduates left the East Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 125 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the East Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was Yorkshire and The Humber

In 2018 to 2019, 71% of graduates and 45% of qualified non-graduates living in Lincoln had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 1,870 graduates and 1,530 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Lincoln. This is compared with the 1,040 graduates and 1,190 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 29% of the graduates had also lived in Lincoln as GCSE pupils, while 71% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Lincoln in 2018 to 2019, 55% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 45% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
